A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TabFSBench and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Original experiments and supporting material can be reliably matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 24 models across 12 datasets and four feature-shift scenarios, including performance, robustness and runtime results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds retraining controls, imputation comparisons, feature-importance analyses, automated feature engineering and high-dimensional evaluations.

M1.justification: The benchmark retains its four feature-removal scenarios, Pearson-based feature ordering and default numerical-mean/categorical-mode imputation. The additions evaluate alternative approaches without introducing a new proposed model or changing the documented default pipeline.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluated high-dimensional datasets: Madelon with 500 features and Nomao with 118 features, extending beyond v1's explicitly acknowledged exclusion of datasets exceeding 100 features. Table 11 also adds feature-type-specific shift scenarios. The constructed Heart scenario in Appendix C is described without corresponding evaluation results.

E2.justification: The original predictor roster remains, but v3 substantially expands the evaluated alternatives: native and random imputation versus mean imputation, CAAFE and OcTree for imputation, and OpenFE, CAAFE and OcTree for feature generation with CatBoost and TabPFN (Tables 8-10). Figure 2 additionally compares original training with training directly on shifted data.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include shifted-data retraining with held-out testing, controlled imputation comparisons, and AutoFE evaluation under single and random shifts. The original accuracy, ROC-AUC, RMSE and normalized performance-gap metrics remain. Newly disclosed sampling and tuning details do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial checks of retraining effects, imputation sensitivity, agreement among four importance measures, AutoFE mitigation and feature-type sensitivity. Appendix H.4 also disaggregates the pooled importance-performance relationship into dataset-specific fits. The original removal-order and runtime analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G.1 newly reports a correlation with p < 0.01 and asserts statistically insignificant differences between importance rankings. Appendix E introduces a final 15-seed statement, but H.1 retains v1's three-seed description, so an actual increase is unresolved. Confidence bands were already present in v1.

E6.justification: The original main performance-gap/ranking tables and all original dataset-specific scores are unchanged. v3 adds substantial results in Figure 2 and Tables 2 and 8-13. For example, new Table 10 reports CatBoost scores of 0.716 for the baseline and 0.845 with CAAFE at 54% random shift.

T1.justification: The feature-set definitions and equations for normalized performance gap and Pearson correlation are retained. The added upper-bound comparison is empirical; no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and three headline observations: limited feature-shift robustness, an importance-degradation relationship, and correlation between closed-environment and shifted performance. Added experiments principally support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of retraining gaps, importance-ranking consistency, AutoFE mitigation, feature-type vulnerability and dataset-specific trajectories. The limitations remove the earlier high-dimensional and imputation-comparison omissions and explicitly discuss exclusion of specialized feature-increment architectures. Appendix C also qualifies how realistic feature-shift datasets should be evaluated.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies Optuna tuning with 100 trials and batch size 1024, capped enumeration of up to 10,000 feature subsets, and native imputation behavior. It adds leaderboard and contribution documentation. Existing hardware, prompts and hyperparameter grids remain; these disclosures alone do not demonstrate changed execution settings.

R1.justification: Focused additions distinguish feature-space shifts from heterogeneous domain adaptation and covariate shift, and introduce AutoFE, TabZilla and newer open-environment references. Several earlier citations are removed. The central positioning against distribution-shift benchmarks remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized rewrites to scenario explanations, Observation 3 and limitations, updates title/author text, and inserts additional appendix sections and an availability statement. The main six-section narrative and much of the original prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds three substantive figures: the retraining comparison, importance-ranking heatmaps and dataset-specific correlation fits, plus eight tables. Original figure images are retained and renumbered, while table typography and placement change, including relocation of the runtime figure.

improvement.justification: The imputation comparisons and high-dimensional evaluations address two explicit v1 limitations, while retraining and importance checks strengthen scrutiny of the benchmark. However, conflicting three-versus-15-seed descriptions, incomplete settings for some new comparisons and insufficiently qualified feature-type interpretations limit confidence in the additions. The evidence supports a useful but limited overall improvement.
